title: Retrospective Analysis of the Maximal Aortic valve Cusp Separation (MACS) as a screening tool for moderate to severe aortic valve stenosis
summary: This study examines previously collected data to evaluate a simple parameter derived from transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) that could potentially rule out significant aortic valve stenosis or, if necessary, guide patients toward further cardiological diagnostics. This is particularly important in preoperative settings, such as in anesthesia clinics.

interventions.name: Patients with aortic stenosis as proven by an transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) in the cardiology echo lab, Charité Campus Virchow Klinikum.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosis of aortic valve stenosis (mild, moderate, or severe) by transthoracic echocardiography performed by an expert in echocardiography.
Exclusion criteria:
1) Age under 18 years.
2) History of aortic valve replacement (prosthetic valve or homograft) or transfemoral aortic valve intervention (TAVI or balloon valvuloplasty).
3) Imaging quality reported as: "poor" or "insufficient".
